# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

</system-reminder>

# Every local src/href in HTML/CSS must exist; nothing may load from another origin (the page is self-contained).
  while IFS= read -r ref; do
    case "$ref" in http://*|https://*|//*) echo "    hotlink: $ref"; bad=1; continue ;; data:*|mailto:*|\#*|"") continue ;; /sign-in|/sign-in\?*|/sign-up|/sign-up\?*) continue ;; esac
    ref="${ref%%[?#]*}"; [ -z "$ref" ] && continue
    [ -e "$SRC/${ref#./}" ] || [ -e "$SRC/${ref#/}" ] || { echo "    missing: $ref"; bad=1; }
  done < <(grep -ohE '(src|href)="[^"]*"' "$SRC/index.html" | sed -E 's/^(src|href)="//; s/"$//' | sort -u)
  while IFS= read -r ref; do
    case "$ref" in http*|//*) echo "    css hotlink: $ref"; bad=1 ;; esac
  done < <(grep -rohE 'url\(["'\'']?[^)"'\'']+' "$SRC" --include=*.css | sed -E "s/^url\(['\"]?//" | sort -u)
  local size; size=$(du -sb "$SRC" | cut -f1)
  [ "$size" -le "$MAX_BYTES" ] || { echo "    src is $size bytes (> $MAX_BYTES)"; bad=1; }
  [ "$bad" = 0 ] || die "site check failed"
  log "site check ok ($(find "$SRC" -type f | wc -l) files, $size bytes)"
}

cmd_build() {
  cmd_check
  rm -rf "$DIST.tmp"; mkdir -p "$DIST.tmp"
  cp -a "$SRC/." "$DIST.tmp/"
  local sha; sha=$(git -C "$HERE" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo nogit)
  # Featured mods (optional): CYRUS_SITE_FEATURED_JSON = a file or https URL of the app's /api/cyrus/featured answer.
  # Empty list or unreadable source = the section is left out; the build never fails because of it.
  if [ -n "${CYRUS_SITE_FEATURED_JSON:-}" ]; then
    node "$HERE/featured.mjs" --in "$DIST.tmp/index.html" --json "$CYRUS_SITE_FEATURED_JSON" ${CYRUS_SITE_FEATURED_ORIGIN:+--origin "$CYRUS_SITE_FEATURED_ORIGIN"} || log "featured section skipped"
  fi
  (cd "$DIST.tmp" && find . -type f ! -name MANIFEST.sha256 -print0 | sort -z | xargs -0 sha256sum > MANIFEST.sha256)
  printf '{"commit":"%s","builtAt":"%s"}\n' "$sha" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" > "$DIST.tmp/release.json"
  rm -rf "$DIST"; mv "$DIST.tmp" "$DIST"
  log "built dist/ (commit $sha)"
}

live_target() { [ -L "$LIVE" ] && readlink -f "$LIVE" || true; }

health_ok() {
  [ -z "$HEALTH_URL" ] && return 0
  local code; code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 10 ${HEALTH_RESOLVE:+-k --resolve "$HEALTH_RESOLVE"} "$HEALTH_URL" || true)

# Off-box backup replication.
#
# Copies the DB dumps, the host-configuration archives and (optionally) the

# not take the backups with it.

# -07-25 and -07-26 and recorded `Result=success` every time, having copied
# nothing anywhere. systemd showed a green unit, the OnFailure=nxeon-alert@ hook
# never fired because nothing failed, and the admin portal had no page that would

#!/bin/bash
# Cyrus OFF-BOX encrypted backup (restic). The primary's /tank is one disk with NO redundancy and node-2 (the
# nightly target of backup-nightly.sh) is the only other copy: this adds a third copy outside both machines.
# Dry run unless --go. NOT INSTALLED, NEVER RUN against a real target by the agent that wrote it.
#
#   scripts/cyrus/backup-offbox.sh [--go] [--only files|db|vm|forget|verify] [--restore-test]
#
# Env (usually /etc/cyrus/offbox.env, root 0600, NEVER in the repo):
#   CYRUS_OFFBOX_REPO       restic repository URL: s3:https://s3.<region>.example/<bucket>/cyrus | sftp:user@host:/path |
#                           rclone:<remote>:<path>. Provider credentials (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID ...) go in the same env file.
#   CYRUS_OFFBOX_PASSFILE   file holding the restic password (root 0600). Keep an offline copy: without it the data is
#                           unrecoverable. The password file is NOT backed up into the repo it unlocks.
#   CYRUS_OFFBOX_KEEP       retention flags (default: --keep-daily 7 --keep-weekly 5 --keep-monthly 6)
#   CYRUS_OFFBOX_SFX=1      also back up the owner's proprietary SFX library (51 GB, first run is slow)
#   CYRUS_OFFBOX_VM=1       also stream the build service data of VM 88001 (read-only ssh tar; no writes on the VM)
#   CYRUS_BACKUP_STAGE      where backup-nightly.sh keeps the newest encrypted DB dump (offbox-queue/)
#   CYRUS_OFFBOX_STATUS     success marker read by launch-check (default /var/lib/cyrus/offbox-last-success)
# What goes where is the inventory in docs/cyrus/07-operations.md ("Backups and restore").

KEEP="${CYRUS_OFFBOX_KEEP:---keep-daily 7 --keep-weekly 5 --keep-monthly 6}"

## 4. Switch the build service from your subscription login to an API key

This must happen **before any public launch**. Run:

```
API_KEY=sk-ant-... bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh
```

This can be combined with step 3. The old env file is kept as `/root/claudebox.env.bak-subscription`, and the login directory is moved aside as `.claude-modbuilder.bak-<ts>`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Smoke | `smoke-readonly.sh service` must show `OK auth api_key` |
| Rollback | The script restores the env file and the login directory automatically if health fails. By hand: copy `claudebox.env.bak-subscription` back, move the login directory back, then `./run.sh <tag>` |

**Must NOT be switched on while the build service runs on your subscription login.** The smoke script and `FLIP=yes` refuse these:

- The launch pair `cyrus_studio_public_enabled` + `cyrus_tok_live`, which lets every verified account build.
- Any paid eval run or bulk builds: the 124-prompt eval set, and the stage-B AI tagging, which also runs on the model.
- `CYRUS_CATALOG_TOOLS` for customers. It adds tool-call tokens to every build.
- Studio "Ask Cyrus" candidate builds for non-preview users. They are builds, so they follow the launch pair.
- `CYRUS_MESHGEN`. It calls a model per asset, and has no caller yet.

Preview accounts may keep testing on the login (as today).

## Observability and backups (r37, built, NOT installed)
`GET /api/cyrus/health` (names the release commit via `CYRUS_RELEASE_COMMIT`), error hook (`CYRUS_ERROR_WEBHOOK_URL`, scrubbed, deduplicated Discord), cost export (`scripts/cyrus/cost-export.sh`), alert rules and checker (`scripts/cyrus/alert-check.sh`, `deploy/cyrus/cyrus-alerts.service`, spend alert `CYRUS_SPEND_ALERT_USD`), uptime list and status-page spec, nightly **encrypted** backup (`scripts/cyrus/backup-nightly.sh`, public-key encryption, remote target, library files opt-in, SFX only enc

## Storage report and alerts (r51, NOT installed)
`scripts/cyrus/storage-report.sh` (read only: `df`, `zpool list`, `du` of Cyrus' directories and backups on the primary and on node-2 over ssh) writes `CYRUS_STORAGE_REPORT` (default `/var/lib/cyrus/storage-report.json`) for the admin Storage tab; nightly via `deploy/cyrus/cyrus-storage-report.{service,timer}` (idle IO, du over `/tank/backup` takes minutes). `scripts/cyrus/alert-check.sh` has a `disk` rule kind; `deploy/cyrus/alert-rules.json` adds `/` and `/tank` on both hosts (80/90 %) and acc

## Incident playbooks (past outages and how not to repeat them)
| Incident | Cause | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Two prod outages 2026-10-01 | raw `npm run build` + restart in the live tree | Deploy only via deploy-staging -> promote-production; builds run on node-2. |
| Primary hard crash 2026-10-06 | parallel agent builds (load 16+, swap full) | All heavy work on node-2 via `devhost`; cap agent builds. |
| Prod DB ownership moved cluster-wide 2026-10-07 | an agent ran `REASSIGN OWNED` | Forbid role/ownership SQL in every agent brief; never give agents prod DB credentials. |
| Root disk full 2026-09-27 (Postgres crashed, prod 500 for about 10 min) | build caches on `/` | Never write to the primary root disk; clear only known-safe caches. |
| `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live prod | pattern kill | Kill by port PID or systemd unit only. |
| `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree could replace prod's node_modules with a self-referential symlink | worktree + symlink | Never `git add -A`; never symlink node_modules; add paths by name. |
| Rollback-incomplete on a revoke mid-update (r38 run) | rollback re-creating an existing parent folder was refused | Fixed; delivery now reports `rollback_incomplete` honestly and restores exact bytes. |
| Stuck at "Compiling" in the prod studio (2026-10) | root cause not found; service answered in 0.4 s, nginx fine | Stream-silence watchdog (30 s, re-attach) in `lib/cyrus/forge.ts`. |
| rc1 type check out of memory (found 2026-10-11, never deployed) | the merged Cyrus tree had never been through `next build`; one structural PrismaClient comparison in `lib/cyrus/host/nxeon.ts` cost ~1.1M types per program, and the whole program needs ~6.3 GB
| A promote that rolled itself back | overloaded primary failed the health check | Quiet hour, no agent builds, retry. |
| Build host VMs could not reach nxeon.cloud (hairpin firewall) | firewall rule, fixed 2026-08-23 | See the Nxeon firewall notes; check this first if flights cannot fetch from the site. |

If a Cyrus build fails for a customer: check `/admin/cyrus/builds/<id>` (engine release record, flight verdict, errors), then the service `/health`; our-side failures are free for the customer (token release). If node-2 is down say so; do not fall back to buil

watch, and what to do when something breaks. Everything here is the owner's to run; nothing in it was executed by the
agent that wrote it.

**The gate for every step:** `scripts/cyrus/launch-check.sh public` (or the admin Launch check tab). It prints GO or
NO-GO for a private beta and for a public launch and names each gap with its fix. Do not take a step marked
"requires GO" while it says NO-GO. `launch-check.sh` is read only and safe to run as often as you like.

## 0. Roles and tools

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Launch GO / NO-GO | `scripts/cyrus/launch-check.sh [beta\|public]`, admin tab Launch check, `smoke-readonly.sh launch` |
| Flags, launch pair, kill switches | `https://<admin host>/admin/cyrus/flags` (typed confirmations `LAUNCH CYRUS` / `CLOSE CYRUS`) |
| Settings (prices, caps, alert thresholds) | admin Audit & settings |
| Builds, live feed, cost, tokens | admin Builds, Live, Cost, Users & tokens, Reconciliation |
| Alerts | Discord channel behind `CYRUS_ALERT_DISCORD_WEBHOOK`; status feed `/var/lib/cyrus/status.json` |
| Logs | `journalctl -u nxeon-web -u nxeon-worker`; VM 88001 `docker logs modbuilder` (read only) |

## 1. Before launch day (all reversible, none customer visible)

1. **Backups first.** Install `cyrus-backup.timer` with `/etc/cyrus/backup-pubkey.asc`, then set the off-box repo
   (`docs/cyrus/07-operations.md`, "Backups and restore"). Run `backup-nightly.sh --go` once, `backup-offbox.sh --go
   --restore-test` once, and do the restore drill. `launch-check` rows `backup-fresh` and `backup-offbox` must PASS.
2. **Alerts.** Install `cyrus-alerts.timer` and `/etc/cyrus/alerts.env` (webhook + read-only DB URL). Post a test:
   `scripts/cyrus/alert-check.sh --dry-run` shows every rule; trigger one real alert on purpose (set
   `cyrus_alert_queue_depth` to 0 for ten minutes, then restore the default).
3. **Legal.** Terms, privacy and AUP published on nxeon.cloud, linked from the sign-in/sign-up page and the landing
   footer (`launch-check` rows `legal-pages`, `legal-linked`). Libraries: only CC0/cleared sound content is visible
   (`CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED` matches the licence ledger).
4. **Prices.** In admin Economy confirm margins; in Audit & settings save a value for every setting `launch-check`
   lists under `placeholders` (saving the default is a decision). Set `cyrus_cost_platform_daily_cap_usd`,
   `cyrus_cost_user_daily_cap_usd`, `cyrus_cost_alert_platform_daily_usd`.
5. **Stripe live mode.** Live secret key and live webhook signing secret in the portal env
   (`STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), webhook endpoint `https://nxeon.cloud/api/stripe/webhook`
   (event `checkout.session.completed`), Cyrus token products created (`scripts/cyrus-tokens-stripe-setup.ts`).
   Rollback: put the test keys back and promote.

## 2. The launch sequence (public)

Run each step, then `launch-check.sh public`, then wait for the stated signal. One step at a time.

| # | Step | Command / place | Signal it worked | Rollback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Freeze: no agent builds, no promotes, quiet hour | n/a | primary load under 2 | none needed |
| 2 | Release on the primary matches the repo you checked | `smoke-readonly.sh service`; compare `/api/cyrus/health` commit | health `ok`, promptVersion equals the repo's | promote the previous release (`promote-production.sh` rollback) |
| 3 | **API key swap** (build service off the owner's subscription login) | `API_KEY=sk-ant-... bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh` (or `TAG=modbuilder:X.Y` to also change the image) | `smoke-readonly.sh service` prints `OK auth api_key`; guard smoke prints `GUARD OK` (recorded in `/var/lib/cyrus/guard-smoke.json`) | the script restores `/root/claudebox.env.bak-subscription` and the login directory if health fails; by hand: copy it back, move `.claude-modbuilder.bak-<ts>` back, `./run.sh <previous tag>` |
| 4 | **Price check** | admin Economy: every plan margin positive after Stripe fees; `launch-check` `placeholders` and `cost-cap` PASS | no WARN in those rows | set the previous values in Audit & settings (history in the audit tab) |
| 5 | **Env flags** the launch needs: `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP`, `CYRUS_STORAGE` (+`CYRUS_STORAGE_ADDONS` only after the card path is tried), `CYRUS_WALLET_PAY`, `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED` as decided | portal env (flag writes are the owner's), then promote or restart web | Flags tab env table shows them `on`; `launch-check` `combos` PASS | remove the line, restart `nxeon-web` |
| 6 | **Canary account** (a normal, non-staff, non-preview-list account with a small wallet): build one small mod end to end while the pair is still OFF using the preview allow-list | add the canary email to `preview_access_emails_modbuilder` | build succeeds, tokens settle, pack installs on the test server | remove the email |
| 7 | Requires GO (public): **flip the launch pair** together: admin Flags > Launch (type `LAUNCH CYRUS`), or `bash /root/agent-notes/set-setting.sh cyrus_studio_public_enabled true && bash /root/agent-notes/set-setting.sh cyrus_tok_live true` | Flags tab shows both on; `launch-check` `pair` PASS | **`CLOSE CYRUS` in Flags** or the two `false` writes; effective on the next request. Running builds finish and settle. |
| 8 | Public canary: a brand new account signs up on cyrus.my, accepts the terms, buys a small token pack (live mode, refund it in Stripe afterwards), builds one mod | `/admin/cyrus/live`, Users & tokens | the ledger shows grant, reserve, spend; Reconciliation clean | as step 7 |
| 9 | Optional: `cyrus_public_enabled=true` (marketing page indexable) and the status page (nginx snippet `deploy/cyrus/nginx-cyrus-status.conf.snippet`, `CYRUS_STATUS_PAGE=1`) | | `/status` shows operational | remove the include, reload nginx |

(`cyrus_ai_gw_kill`), mod networking off. Use the build pause first in any incident: it stops new spend and keeps
installs, downloads and the wallet working.

## 3. First 24 hours: who watches what

One person on point (the owner) with the Discord alert channel open. Suggested rhythm: every 15 min for the first
2 h, hourly until the first night, then at 06:00 and 18:00.

| Look at | Healthy | Act when |
|---|---|---|
| Admin Live feed + Builds | success rate above 80 %, wait under 2 min | failure rate alert, or 3 identical errors: incident "bad build shipped" / "AI backend down" |
| Cost tab | under `cyrus_cost_alert_platform_daily_usd`, per-build average near $0.30 | spend spike: incident "cost spike" |
| Users & tokens + Reconciliation | every spend has a ledger row, no negative balance | ledger alert: incident "token ledger discrepancy" |
| Discord alerts | silent | any CRITICAL: run the matching section below |
| Stripe dashboard (live) | webhooks 2xx | failures: incident "Stripe webhook failure" |
| `launch-check.sh public` at +1 h, +6 h, +24 h | GO | any new FAIL |
| Disk `/` (89 % on 2026-10-14) and `/tank` | under 80 % | clear logs/caches on `/` BEFORE launch; never a build on `/` |

## 4. Incident runbook

For every incident: note the time, post in the owner channel, set the build pause if money or customer data is at risk,
fix, write the cause in `docs/cyrus/07-operations.md` playbook table.

### AI backend down (`ai-backend-burst` alert, or builds fail with `ai_unavailable` / session limit)
1. Admin Builds: confirm the errorCode and that it is not one prompt. `curl 127.0.0.1:7340/health` from the primary.
2. Pause builds (Flags > global build pause). Failures are free for customers (tokens released), but retries burn goodwill.
3. Key problem (auth errors, 401/403, billing): rotate or top up the API key in the Anthropic console, then
   `API_KEY=... bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh`. Provider outage: wait, post to the status feed, resume.
4. Resume, canary one build, watch the failure-rate alert clear.

### Build backlog (`queue-depth` alert: more than `cyrus_alert_queue_depth` queued, or oldest over 15 min)
1. Builds tab: are builds running (service concurrency) or stuck? `health` shows `running` and `queued`.
2. Stuck at one stage: restart the build service container from VM 88001 (owner action), queued builds are re-picked.
3. Genuine load: leave the pause OFF only if wait stays under 10 min; otherwise pause and let it drain, tell users.
4. Check node-2 disk and the test-flight host if flights are the slow stage.

### Cost spike (`ai-spend-24h` critical)
1. Cost tab: by account, by prompt kind, repair share. One account: suspend or set `cyrus_cost_user_daily_cap_usd`.
2. Platform wide: lower `cyrus_cost_platform_daily_cap_usd` (new builds refused with 503 above it), or pause builds.
3. If repair share jumped, the last image or prompt change is suspect: run the eval gate, roll the image back
   (`TAG=<previous> bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh`).

### Bad build shipped (customer reports a crash / a mod breaks servers)
1. Find the build in admin Builds (engine release record, flight verdict). Check whether the flight gate ran.
2. Stop the spread: hide/take down the community page if published (Community tab), disable the mod on affected
   servers through the lifecycle tools; the delivery path rolls back exact bytes.
3. If the cause is the engine: pause builds, roll the image back, re-run the eval gate, then resume. Credit affected
   accounts through Users & tokens (comp/refund, audited).

### Token ledger discrepancy (`ledger-anomaly` critical)
1. Reconciliation tab names the accounts. The ledger is append-only and idempotent: the ledger is the truth, the
   balance is derived. Never edit rows by hand.
2. Pause builds if more than a handful of accounts differ (a settle bug). For one account use an audited admin
   grant/revoke to correct, never SQL.
3. Stale reservations (over 2 h) mean a settle job died: restart `nxeon-worker`; reservations release on retry.

### Stripe webhook failure (`webhook-failures`, or Stripe dashboard shows non-2xx)
1. Stripe dashboard: the response code and body. 400 = signing secret mismatch (live vs test secret, the usual cause
   after the live swap); 5xx = web down; timeout = primary overloaded.
2. Fix the secret in the portal env and promote/restart. Then resend the failed events from the Stripe dashboard; the
   handler is idempotent by session id.
3. Check Reconciliation for paid-but-ungranted tokens before closing.

### Data-subject request (access / export / erasure)
1. Verify identity through the account email, never a ticket claim alone. Owner sign-off before replying.
2. Export: the account data export (`/api/account/export`) plus Cyrus data (projects, ledger) from admin Users & tokens.
3. Erasure: admin GDPR erase (`CYRUS_GDPR_ERASE` on, typed confirmation). It does not touch the append-only ledger
   rows needed for accounting (financial records); say so in the reply. Backups age out under the retention in the
   backups section (14 daily, 8 weekly on node-2; 7/5/6 off-box), so state a 90 day horizon.
4. Log the request and its completion in the audit tab.

## 5. On-call cheat sheet

```
scripts/cyrus/launch-check.sh public           # GO / NO-GO with fixes (read only)
scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh service         # build service: auth, image, queue
scripts/cyrus/alert-check.sh --dry-run          # every alert rule, nothing posted
curl -s 127.0.0.1:7340/health | head -c 400     # build service raw
systemctl status nxeon-web nxeon-worker cyrus-alerts.timer
journalctl -u nxeon-web --since -15min | grep -i cyrus | tail
```

| Symptom | First move | Then |
|---|---|---|
| Studio won't load | `curl https://cyrus.my/api/cyrus/health` | `systemctl status nxeon-web`; `nginx -t`; Cloudflare status |
| Builds all fail | pause builds | AI backend down section |
| Builds slow | `health` queued/running | backlog section |
| Money looks wrong | pause builds | ledger section; never SQL |
| Customer reports crash | find build | bad build section |
| Disk alert | `df -h / /tank` | clear known caches on `/`; never build on `/` |
| Cert alert | `certbot certificates` | `certbot renew`; check Cloudflare edge cert |
| Backup stale | `cat /tank/cyrus-backups/LAST_SUCCESS` (node-2) | `systemctl status cyrus-backup`; run `backup-nightly.sh --go` |

Rules that still apply: never build or edit in `/opt/nxeon`; never `pkill -f`; never run role/ownership SQL; never
print `.env`; do not reply to support tickets without the owner's sign-off.
